messages:
maya.marketing: Hey design — launching lightweight benchmark blog + webinar next week. Need a small creative pack fast: 2 hero tiles (one long, one square), 1 simplified seq-diagram (latency vs tokens), plus a one-slide infographic version. Can design take this on with 48hr turnaround?

rachel.design: Can do if we scope tightly. Clarify szs: long hero 1200x628, square 800x800? And does the seq-diagram need callouts for batching/kv-cache?

sam.pm: Yes sizes fine. Diagram: highlight three levers — batching, cache, quantization — with simple icons and a redwood color palette. Keep it single-slide readable at 800px width for blog. Infographic is a condensed version of the diagram for a webinar slide.

jo.content: Copy ready. Short headline options: 
- "Serve smarter: cost & latency tradeoffs"
- "Optimize inference: batching, cache, quant"
I'll add 2 CTA variations in figma comments.

rachel.design: Ok will produce wireframes first. Request: exportable SVG for diagram (no embedded fonts), transparent PNGs @2x for tiles, and a short usage note (one para) saying when to use the long vs square hero. Also add component variants in the file.

maya.marketing: Also include 1 dark-mode variant for social and a version with no logos for partner syndication. Legal: avoid using the phrase "production-grade" without approval.

figma-bot: File created by rachel.design 1 frames	| comments enabled	

rachel.design: Timeline: draft wireframes in 24h, first comps within 36h, final assets in 48h. I'll tag sam + maya in Figma for review.

sam.pm: Works for me. Please prioritize the seq-diagram and long hero first. I'll prep the webinar slide template to fit the infographic dimensions.

jo.content: Tiny ask: include 1 alt-text suggestion per image in the Figma comments so I can push to CMS quickly.

maya.marketing: Thanks all 44D I'll schedule a 30-min review slot after the first comps. Keep the file name prefixed with "launch-slice/" so we can find it in the repo.

rachel.design: Will do. If legal flags phrasing, we'll keep copy generic. Posting frames shortly.
